verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses:

verses.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：耶和华的节期，你们要宣告为圣会的节期。
verses.en: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them, ‘These are the Lord’s appointed times which you must proclaim as holy assemblies—my appointed times.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “these are them, my appointed times.” sn The term מוֹעֵד (moʿed, rendered “appointed time” here) can refer to either a time or place of meeting. See the note on “tent of meeting” (אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד, ʾohel moʿed) in Lev 1:1.
verses.commentary:
23:2 "The Lord's appointed times" YHWH set special times for His people to
congregate at a central worship site and to commemorate His character and past acts on their behalf. They were ways
to train the next generation of Israelites (i.e., Deut. 6:1-9; see full note online).

Those special days are also called "holy convocations" (cf. Lev. 23:2,4,7,21,27,35). This name (i.e.,
"holy convocations") occurs only

- in this chapter, eleven times

- Exod. 12:16, twice

- Numbers 28:29, six times

For a good discussion of "holy" see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY and NIDOTTE, vol. 3, pp. 877-887, esp. p. 880, (g).

These special feasts (and one fast day) may be in view in Gen. 1:14, as the purpose of the great night
light and sun.

There are three annual feasts that must be attended by all males (i.e., those who live close enough, which
reflects a later period) at the Tabernacle or later at the Temple in Jerusalem.

There are several of these lists of feast days and they are difficult to coordinate because of

- different names

- brief texts

- historical developments

- use of two calendars (i.e., sacred and civil) by ancient Israel

verses.zh: 六日要做工，第七日是圣安息日，当有圣会；你们甚么工都不可做。这是在你们一切的住处向耶和华守的安息日。
verses.en: “‘Six days work may be done, but on the seventh day there must be a Sabbath of complete rest,[NOTE:1] a holy assembly. You must not do any work; it is a Sabbath to the Lord in all the places where you live.
notes: This is a superlative expression, emphasizing the full and all inclusive rest of the Sabbath and certain festival times throughout the chapter (see B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 155). Cf. ASV “a sabbath of solemn rest.”
verses.commentary:
23:3 "but on the seventh day there is a sabbath of complete rest" This special weekly time of worship goes back to

- Gen. 2:1-2

- Exod. 16:27-30; 20:8-11; 23:12; 31:12-16

Surprisingly it is discussed very little in this context (Lev. 23:3 only). Probably because the Sabbath guidelines
and purpose were so well known. See Roland deVaux Ancient Israel, pp. 475-493. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: SABBATH (OT) and
NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp. 1157-1161.

Notice that some holy days had complete rest but others allowed some labor

- complete rest ‒ Lev. 23:3,7,28,30-32

- limited labor (i.e. preparing for the feast, but not vocational work) ‒ Lev. 23:8,21,25,35,36

▣ "in all your dwellings" The biblical material about Israel's feasts and special days developed over time.
It is hard to know if the text is a later editorial addition or idiom.

- wilderness wandering period with Tabernacle (i.e., Exod. 12:20; Num. 35:29)

- early period after crossing the Jordan (i.e., Lev. 3:16-17; 7:26; 23:3,14,17,31)

- later period with Temple (i.e., Ezek. 6:6)

- still later to Jewish settlement outside of Palestine

Maybe the best way to deal with a phrase like this is to translate it as a dynamic equivalent ‒ NIV, NEB,
"wherever you live"; TEV, "no matter where you live."

verses.zh: 耶和华的节期，就是你们到了日期要宣告为圣会的，乃是这些。」
verses.en: “‘These are the Lord’s appointed times, holy assemblies, which you must proclaim at their appointed time.
verses.commentary:
23:4-8 This is the discussion of the combined feasts of

- Passover (1 day; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: PASSOVER; NIDOTTE, vol. 3, pp. 642-644, vol. 4, pp. 1043-1045)

- Unleavened Bread (1 week; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FEASTS OF ISRAEL, I, D, 1, c)

- see Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, pp. 484-493

verses.zh: 「正月十四日，黄昏的时候，是耶和华的逾越节。
verses.en: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, at twilight,[NOTE:1] is a Passover offering to the Lord.
notes: See B. A. Levine, Leviticus (JPSTC), 156, for a full discussion of the issues raised in this verse. The rabbinic tradition places the slaughter of Passover offerings between approximately 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m., not precisely at twilight. Moreover, the term פֶּסַח (pesakh) may mean “protective offering” rather than “Passover offering,” although they amount to about the same thing in the historical context of the exodus from Egypt (see Exod 11-12). tn Heb “between the two evenings,” either designating the time between the setting of the sun and the true darkness of night or the time between the descent of the sun from high noon to sunset; the translation “at twilight” accepts the first interpretation. Cf. KJV, ASV “at even”; NAB “at the evening twilight.”
verses.commentary:
23:5 "the first month" Remember Israel used a lunar calendar. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE CALENDARS.

▣ "at twilight" This is literally "between the two evenings." The Israelites made a distinction between the
setting of the sun and the appearance of the first star (cf. Exod. 12:6; Num. 9:3,5,11; Deut. 16:4,6). Note
the same type imagery in Lev. 23:32.

▣ "Passover" The Feast of Passover (i.e., Exodus 12) is later combined with the Feast of Unleavened Bread
(cf. Lev. 23:6) into one eight-day feast (cf. Deut. 16:1-8).

verses.zh: 这月十五日是向耶和华守的无酵节；你们要吃无酵饼七日。
verses.en: Then on the fifteenth day of the same month[NOTE:1] will be the Feast of Unleavened Bread to the Lord; seven days you must eat unleavened bread.
notes: Heb “to this month.”
verses.commentary:
23:6 "feast" This Hebrew NOUN (BDB 290) means "festival gathering" (i.e., at the
Tabernacle/Temple) or "pilgrim feast." This same root in Arabic denotes the annual Muslim pilgrimage (Hag) to Mecca.

▣ "for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread" This would have been grain from the previous year's harvest.

verses.zh: 第一日当有圣会，甚么劳碌的工都不可做；
verses.en: On the first day there will be a holy assembly for you; you must not do any regular work.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “work of service”; KJV “servile work”; NASB “laborious work”; TEV “daily work.”

verses.zh: 要将火祭献给耶和华七日。第七日是圣会，甚么劳碌的工都不可做。」
verses.en: You must present a gift to the Lord for seven days, and the seventh day is a holy assembly; you must not do any regular work.’”
verses.commentary:
23:8 "you shall not do any laborious work" This phrase is repeated in Lev. 23:8,21,25,35,36. The Jewish
Study Bible, p. 262, suggests that there is a total ban on work on the Sabbath (Lev. 23:3) or Day of Atonement (Lev. 23:28,30),
but for the other feast days, preparations for the feast were allowed (cf. Exod. 12:16). People could not do their normal work activities.

verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses:
verses.commentary:
23:9-14 This is the discussion of the initial offering of first fruits. It is uncertain how Lev. 23:9-14 relates to 23:15-21.
I think one occurred at the beginning of the barley harvest (i.e., Feast of Unleavened Bread; see Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel,
pp. 490-493) and the next at the conclusion of the wheat harvest (i.e., Pentecost); see NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp. 21, #2; 1272.

verses.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：你们到了我赐给你们的地，收割庄稼的时候，要将初熟的庄稼一捆带给祭司。
verses.en: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them, ‘When you enter the land that I am about to give to you and you gather in its harvest,[NOTE:1] then you must bring the sheaf of the first portion of your harvest[NOTE:2] to the priest,
notes: Heb “and you harvest its harvest.”
Heb “the sheaf of the first of your harvest.”

verses.zh: 他要把这一捆在耶和华面前摇一摇，使你们得蒙悦纳。祭司要在安息日的次日把这捆摇一摇。
verses.en: and he must wave the sheaf before the Lord to be accepted for your benefit[NOTE:1]—on the day after the Sabbath the priest is to wave it.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “for your acceptance.”
See Lev 7:30 for a note on the “waving” of a “wave offering.”
verses.commentary:
23:11-12 "wave" See notes at Lev. 7:30 and NIDOTTE, vol. 3, pp. 64-65.

23:11 "for you to be accepted" This NOUN (BDB 953) is used several times in Leviticus (cf. Lev. 1:3; 19:5;
22:19,20,21,29; 23:11). It is hard to determine if the "acceptance" is of the appropriate sacrifice or the person offering the sacrifice
(see NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 413). Either way, it shows the essence of Leviticus—how to make sinful Israelites acceptable for fellowship
with a "holy" God.

▣ "on the day after the sabbath" This would refer to our "Sunday" (cf. Lev. 23:15). This is the day Jesus
rose from the dead. The first fruit of the resurrection. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE RESURRECTION.

verses.zh: 摇这捆的日子，你们要把一岁、没有残疾的公绵羊羔献给耶和华为燔祭。
verses.en: On the day you wave the sheaf you must also offer[NOTE:1] a flawless yearling lamb[NOTE:2] for a burnt offering to the Lord,
notes: Heb “And you shall make in the day of your waving the sheaf.”
Heb “a flawless lamb, a son of its year”; KJV “of the first year”; NLT “a year-old male lamb.”
verses.commentary:
23:12 "without defect" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: WITHOUT BLEMISH.

▣ "a burnt offering" See notes at Leviticus 1.

verses.zh: 同献的素祭，就是调油的细面伊法十分之二，作为馨香的火祭，献给耶和华。同献的奠祭，要酒一欣四分之一。
verses.en: along with its grain offering, two-tenths of an ephah of[NOTE:1] choice wheat flour[NOTE:2] mixed with olive oil, as a gift to the Lord, a soothing aroma,[NOTE:3] and its drink offering, one-fourth of a hin of wine.[NOTE:4]
notes: See the note on Lev 5:11.
See the note on Lev 2:1.
See the note on Lev 1:9.
Heb “wine, one-fourth of the hin.” A pre-exilic hin is about 3.6 liters (= ca. 1 gallon), so one-fourth of a hin would be about 1 quart (1 liter).
verses.commentary:
23:13 "grain offering" See notes at Leviticus 2.

▣ "ephah. . .hin" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE WEIGHTS AND VOLUMES.

▣ "a soothing aroma" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: A SOOTHING AROMA.

▣ "libation" This was a liquid offering (cf. Lev. 23:13,18,37; NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 115, #3).

▣ "wine" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: WINE AND STRONG DRINK.

verses.zh: 无论是饼，是烘的子粒，是新穗子，你们都不可吃，直等到把你们献给　神的供物带来的那一天才可以吃。这在你们一切的住处作为世世代代永远的定例。」
verses.en: You must not eat bread, roasted grain, or fresh grain until this very day,[NOTE:1] until you bring the offering to your God. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations[NOTE:2] in all the places where you live.
notes: Heb “until the bone of this day.”
Heb “for your generations.”
verses.commentary:
23:14 This giving of the first fruits was a symbol of YHWH's ownership of all crops, as the Sabbath was
a symbol of all property belonging to YHWH! We are stewards, not owners! See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TITHES IN THE MOSAIC
LEGISLATION and SPECIAL TOPIC: TITHING.

The new crop could not be eaten until the appropriate offering (Lev. 23:13) to YHWH (Lev. 23:14).

- the wave offering of the first fruits

- a one year old lamb

- Grain offering

- drink offering (cf. Lev. 23:13,18,37)

▣ "perpetual statute" See the
SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam) and
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S
REVELATION; also see NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 349.

These two words also appear in Lev. 23:21 and 41. The term 'olam has several connotations. Here,
"age abiding," but the OT has been superceded. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO OT COVENANT PROMISES SEEM SO DIFFERENT FROM NT COVENANT PROMISES?

verses.zh: 「你们要从安息日的次日，献禾捆为摇祭的那日算起，要满了七个安息日。
verses.en: “‘You must count for yourselves seven weeks from the day after the Sabbath, from the day you bring the wave-offering sheaf; they must be complete weeks.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “seven Sabbaths, they shall be complete.” The disjunctive accent under “Sabbaths” precludes the translation “seven complete Sabbaths” (as NASB, NIV; cf. NAB, NRSV, NLT). The text is somewhat awkward, which may explain why the LXX tradition is confused here, either adding “you shall count” again at the end of the verse, or leaving out “they shall be,” or keeping “they shall be” and adding “to you.”
verses.commentary:
23:15-21 This is the discussion of the festival at the end of the harvest season. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FEASTS OF ISRAEL;
Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, pp. 493-495.

The offerings are similar to the ones at the beginning of the harvest (Lev. 23:13), but more extensive.

- two loaves of bread for each family/village (Lev. 23:17)

- seven one-year old lambs (Lev. 23:18)

- one bull (Lev. 23:18) for a burnt offering

- #2 and 3 with accompanying grain and drink offerings (cf. Lev. 23:13; see NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 115)

- one male goat (Lev. 23:19) for a sin offering

- two one-year old lambs (Lev. 23:19) for a peace offering

Numbers 28-29 deal much more specifically about the timing of these sacrifices.

23:15 "seven" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE.

verses.zh: 到第七个安息日的次日，共计五十天，又要将新素祭献给耶和华。
verses.en: You must count 50 days—until the day after the seventh Sabbath—and then[NOTE:1] you must present a new grain offering to the Lord.
notes: Heb “and.” In the translation “then” is supplied to clarify the sequence.
verses.commentary:
23:16 "a new grain offering" This was distinct from the first fruit barley offering of Lev. 23:9-14. This
was a grain offering from the new crop (i.e., wheat).

verses.zh: 要从你们的住处取出细面伊法十分之二，加酵，烤成两个摇祭的饼，当作初熟之物献给耶和华。
verses.en: From the places where you live you must bring two loaves of[NOTE:1] bread for a wave offering; they must be made from two-tenths of an ephah of fine wheat flour, baked with yeast,[NOTE:2] as firstfruits to the Lord.
notes: Smr, LXX, Syriac, Tg. Onq., and Tg. Ps.-J. insert the word חַלּוֹת (khallot, “loaves”; cf. Lev 2:4 and the note there). Even though “loaves” is not explicit in the MT, the number “two” suggests that these are discrete units, not just a measure of flour, so “loaves” should be assumed even in the MT.
Heb “with leaven.” The noun “leaven” is traditional in English versions (cf. KJV, ASV, NASB, NRSV), but “yeast” is more commonly used today.
verses.commentary:
23:17 "baked with leaven" This shows that leaven was not always forbidden in sacrifices (cf. Lev. 7:13-14).
It is not always a symbol of evil. Sometimes it is imagery for "penetration and permeation." See
SPECIAL TOPIC: LEAVEN.

verses.zh: 又要将一岁、没有残疾的羊羔七只、公牛犊一只、公绵羊两只，和饼一同奉上。这些与同献的素祭和奠祭要作为燔祭献给耶和华，就是作馨香的火祭献给耶和华。
verses.en: Along with the loaves of bread,[NOTE:1] you must also present seven flawless yearling lambs,[NOTE:2] one young bull,[NOTE:3] and two rams.[NOTE:4] They are to be a burnt offering to the Lord along with their grain offering[NOTE:5] and drink offerings, a gift of a soothing aroma to the Lord.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “And you shall present on the bread.”
Heb “seven flawless lambs, sons of a year.”
Heb “and one bull, a son of a herd.”
Smr and LXX add “flawless.”
Heb “and their grain offering.”
See the note on Lev 1:9.
verses.commentary:
23:18 "without defect" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: WITHOUT BLEMISH.

▣ "a burnt offering" See Leviticus 1.

▣ "a grain offering" See Leviticus 2.

▣ "a soothing aroma" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: A SOOTHING AROMA.

verses.zh: 你们要献一只公山羊为赎罪祭，两只一岁的公绵羊羔为平安祭。
verses.en: You must also offer[NOTE:1] one male goat[NOTE:2] for a sin offering and two yearling lambs for a peace-offering sacrifice,
notes: Heb “And you shall make.”
Heb “a he-goat of goats.”
verses.commentary:
23:19 "a sin offering" See Leviticus 4.

▣ "a peace offering" See Leviticus 3.

verses.zh: 祭司要把这些和初熟麦子做的饼一同作摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇；这是献与耶和华为圣物归给祭司的。
verses.en: and the priest is to wave them—the two lambs[NOTE:1]—along with the bread of the firstfruits, as a wave offering before the Lord; they will be holy to the Lord for the priest.
notes: Smr and LXX have the Hebrew article on “lambs.” The syntax of this verse is difficult. The object of the verb (two lambs) is far removed from the verb itself (shall wave) in the MT, and the preposition עַל (ʿal, “upon”), rendered “along with” in this verse, is also added to the far removed subject (literally, “upon [the] two lambs”; see B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 159). It is clear, however, that the two lambs and the loaves (along with their associated grain and drink offerings) constituted the “wave offering,” which served as the prebend “for the priest.” Burnt and sin offerings (vv. 18-19a) were not included in this (see Lev 7:11-14, 28-36).

verses.zh: 当这日，你们要宣告圣会；甚么劳碌的工都不可做。这在你们一切的住处作为世世代代永远的定例。
verses.en: “‘On this very day you must proclaim an assembly; it is to be a holy assembly for you.[NOTE:1] You must not do any regular work. This is a perpetual statute in all the places where you live throughout your generations.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And you shall proclaim [an assembly] in the bone of this day; a holy assembly it shall be to you” (see the remarks in B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 160, and the remarks on the LXX rendering in J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 367).
Heb “for your generations.”

verses.zh: 「在你们的地收割庄稼，不可割尽田角，也不可拾取所遗落的；要留给穷人和寄居的。我是耶和华―你们的　神。」
verses.en: When you gather in the harvest[NOTE:1] of your land, you must not completely harvest the corner of your field,[NOTE:2] and you must not gather up the gleanings of your harvest. You must leave them for the poor and the resident foreigner.[NOTE:3] I am the Lord your God.’”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “And when you harvest the harvest.”
Heb “you shall not complete the corner of your field in your harvest.”
On the Hebrew גֵּר (ger, “resident foreigner”) see notes at Exod 12:19 and Deut 29:11. On the privilege of gleaning see also Lev 19:10; 23:22; Deut 14:29; 24:19-21.
verses.commentary:
23:22 This refers to "gleaning." See note at Lev. 19:9-10.

The needy and the alien refer to those who have no land and must work for others for their sustenance.
God (uniquely in the ANE) cares for the powerless and disenfranchised.

verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses:
verses.commentary:
23:23 The footnote in the JB, p. 161, suggests this verse is referring to a monthly lunar festival. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FEASTS OF ISRAEL.

verses.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：七月初一，你们要守为圣安息日，要吹角作纪念，当有圣会。
verses.en: “Tell the Israelites, ‘In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you must have a complete rest, a memorial announced by loud horn blasts,[NOTE:1] a holy assembly.
notes: Heb “a memorial of loud blasts.” Although the term for “horn” does not occur here, allowing for the possibility that vocal “shouts” of acclamation are envisioned (see P. J. Budd, Leviticus [NCBC], 325), the “blast” of the shofar (a trumpet made from a ram’s “horn”) is most likely what is intended. On this occasion, the loud blasts on the horn announced the coming of the new year on the first day of the seventh month (see the explanations in J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 387, and B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 160).
verses.commentary:
23:24-25 This refers to the "New Year" celebration called Rosh Hashanah (cf. Num. 10:9-10; 29:1-6; see
Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, pp. 502-506). It was held on the first day of the seventh month. The New Year's
celebration has several problems.

- Israel's new year may have begun in the spring or autumn (possibly ancient Israel used two calendars, sacred and civil).

- This feast is not called "New Year" by Josephus or Philo.

- Nehemiah 8:1-12 does not mention a "new year" feast at all.

- In Leviticus 23 it is not called "New Year" feast, nor in Num. 29:1-6.

It surely was meant to begin a period of preparation for the Day of Atonement on the tenth of the seventh month.

- Trumpets ‒ seventh month, first day

- Day of Atonement ‒ seventh month, tenth day

- Feast of Booths ‒ seventh month, fifteenth day

23:24 "blowing of trumpets" See parallel in Num. 29:1-6. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: HORNS USED BY ISRAEL.

verses.zh: 甚么劳碌的工都不可做；要将火祭献给耶和华。」
verses.en: You must not do any regular work, but[NOTE:1] you must present a gift to the Lord.’”
notes: Heb “and.” The Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) can be considered to have adversative force here (cf. KJV, NASB, NIV).

verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses:
verses.commentary:
23:26-32 This annual fast day (i.e., "humble your souls") for unintentional sins of the people, the priest, and
the Tabernacle, was discussed in detail in Leviticus 16 (see notes there; see Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel,
pp. 507-510).

verses.zh: 「七月初十是赎罪日；你们要守为圣会，并要刻苦己心，也要将火祭献给耶和华。
verses.en: “The[NOTE:1] tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement.[NOTE:2] It is to be a holy assembly for you, and you must humble yourselves[NOTE:3] and present a gift to the Lord.
notes: Heb “Surely the tenth day” or perhaps “Precisely the tenth day.” The Hebrew adverbial particle אַךְ (ʾakh) is left untranslated by most recent English versions; cf. however NASB “On exactly the tenth day.”
See the description of this day and its regulations in Lev 16 and the notes there.
Heb “you shall humble your souls.” See the note on Lev 16:29 above.
verses.commentary:
23:27 "you shall humble your souls" The VERB (BDB 776, KB 853) is used here and in Lev. 16:31 in
connection to the national fast Day of Atonement. Israel was to contemplate her violation of YHWH's character and laws, probably
by fasting, praying, hearing the law, and meditation.

verses.zh: 当这日，甚么工都不可做；因为是赎罪日，要在耶和华―你们的　神面前赎罪。
verses.en: You must not do any work on this particular day,[NOTE:1] because it is a day of atonement to make atonement for yourselves[NOTE:2] before the Lord your God.
notes: Heb “in the bone of this day.”
Heb “on you [plural]”; cf. NASB, NRSV “on your behalf.”

verses.zh: 当这日，凡不刻苦己心的，必从民中剪除。
verses.en: Indeed,[NOTE:1] any person who does not behave with humility on this particular day will be cut off from his people.[NOTE:2]
notes: The particular כִּי (ki) is taken in an asseverative sense here (“Indeed,” see the NJPS translation).
Heb “it [i.e., that person; literally “soul,” feminine] shall be cut off from its peoples [plural]”; NLT “from the community.”
verses.commentary:
23:29 "he shall be cut off from his people" See full note at Lev. 7:20.

In Lev. 23:30 this phrase is parallel to "I will destroy from among his people." This implies a divine taking of life.

verses.zh: 凡这日做甚么工的，我必将他从民中除灭。
verses.en: As for any person[NOTE:1] who does any work on this particular day, I will exterminate[NOTE:2] that person from the midst of his people[NOTE:3]—
notes: Heb “And any person.”
See HALOT 3 s.v. I אבד hif. Cf. KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT “destroy”; CEV “wipe out.”
Heb “its people” (“its” is feminine to agree with “person,” literally “soul,” which is feminine in Hebrew; cf. v. 29).

verses.zh: 你们甚么工都不可做。这在你们一切的住处作为世世代代永远的定例。
verses.en: you must not do any work! This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations[NOTE:1] in all the places where you live.
notes: Heb “for your generations.”

verses.zh: 你们要守这日为圣安息日，并要刻苦己心。从这月初九日晚上到次日晚上，要守为安息日。」
verses.en: It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you must humble yourselves on the ninth day of the month in the evening, from evening until evening you must observe your Sabbath.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “you shall rest your Sabbath.”
verses.commentary:
23:32 "ninth month" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE CALENDARS.

▣ "you shall keep your sabbath" This is a combination of the VERB (BDB 991, KB 1407)
for "rest" and the NOUN (BDB 992) "sabboth" or "rest." The LXX has "you shall sabbatize on your sabbaths."
REB, "you shall keep your sabbath rest."

verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses:

verses.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：这七月十五日是住棚节，要在耶和华面前守这节七日。
verses.en: “Tell the Israelites, ‘On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Feast of Shelters[NOTE:1] for seven days to the Lord.
notes: The rendering “booths” (cf. NAB, NASB, NRSV) is probably better than the traditional “tabernacles” in light of the meaning of the term סֻכָּה (sukkah, “hut, booth”), but “booths” are frequently associated with trade shows and craft fairs in contemporary American English. The nature of the celebration during this feast (see the following verses) as a commemoration of the wanderings of the Israelites after they left Egypt suggests that a translation like “shelters” is more appropriate.
verses.commentary:
23:34-44 "the Feast of Booths" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FEASTS OF ISRAEL, I, D, 3 and NIDOTTE, vol. 3, pp. 249-251, esp. p. 250, #3, c.

verses.zh: 第一日当有圣会，甚么劳碌的工都不可做。
verses.en: On the first day is a holy assembly; you must do no regular work.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “work of service”; KJV “servile work”; NASB “laborious work”; TEV “daily work.”

verses.zh: 七日内要将火祭献给耶和华。第八日当守圣会，要将火祭献给耶和华。这是严肃会，甚么劳碌的工都不可做。
verses.en: For seven days you must present a gift to the Lord. On the eighth day there is to be a holy assembly for you, and you must present a gift to the Lord. It is a solemn assembly day;[NOTE:1] you must not do any regular work.
notes: The Hebrew term עֲצֶרֶת (ʿatseret) “solemn assembly [day]” derives from a root associated with restraint or closure. It could refer either to the last day as “closing special assembly” day of the festival (e.g., NIV11) or a special day of restraint expressed in a “solemn assembly” (e.g., NRSV); cf. NLT “a solemn closing assembly.”

verses.zh: 「这是耶和华的节期，就是你们要宣告为圣会的节期；要将火祭、燔祭、素祭、祭物，并奠祭，各归各日，献给耶和华。
verses.en: “‘These are the appointed times of the Lord that you must proclaim as holy assemblies to present a gift to the Lord—burnt offering, grain offering, sacrifice, and drink offerings,[NOTE:1] each day according to its regulation,[NOTE:2]
notes: The LXX has “[their] burnt offerings, and their sacrifices, and their drink offerings.”
Heb “a matter of a day in its day”; NAB “as prescribed for each day”; NRSV, NLT “each on its proper day.”
verses.commentary:
23:37 "each day's matter on its own day" This may refer to the different sacrifices offered on each day
(see Numbers 28-29, which focuses on these sacrifices).

verses.zh: 这是在耶和华的安息日以外，又在你们的供物和所许的愿，并甘心献给耶和华的以外。
verses.en: besides[NOTE:1] the Sabbaths of the Lord and all your gifts, votive offerings, and freewill offerings which you must give to the Lord.
notes: Heb “from to separation.” See BDB 94 s.v. בַּד 1.e for an explanation of this phrase. This phrase is repeated in front of each of the four items in this verse in the Hebrew text, but these have not been translated into English for stylistic reasons. Cf. KJV, NASB “besides”; NRSV “apart from.”
verses.commentary:
23:38 TEV expresses the sense of the verse well: "These festivals are in addition to the regular Sabbaths,
and these offerings are in addition to your regular gifts, your offerings as fulfillment of vows, and your freewill offerings
that you give to the Lord."

verses.zh: 「你们收藏了地的出产，就从七月十五日起，要守耶和华的节七日。第一日为圣安息；第八日也为圣安息。
verses.en: “‘On[NOTE:1] the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you gather in the produce of the land, you must celebrate a pilgrim festival of the Lord for seven days. On the first day is a complete rest and on the eighth day is complete rest.
notes: Heb “Surely on the fifteenth day.” The Hebrew adverbial particle אַךְ (ʾakh) is left untranslated by most recent English versions; however, cf. NASB “On exactly the fifteenth day.”

verses.zh: 第一日要拿美好树上的果子和棕树上的枝子，与茂密树的枝条并河旁的柳枝，在耶和华―你们的　神面前欢乐七日。
verses.en: On the first day you must take for yourselves branches from majestic trees[NOTE:1]—palm branches, branches of leafy trees, and willows of the brook—and you must rejoice before the Lord your God for seven days.
notes: Heb “fruit of majestic trees,” but the following terms and verses define what is meant by this expression. For extensive remarks on the celebration of this festival in history and tradition see B. A. Levine, Leviticus (JPSTC), 163; J. E. Hartley, Leviticus (WBC), 389-90; and P. J. Budd, Leviticus (NCBC), 328-29.
verses.commentary:
23:40 This verse is the origin of the title "Feast of Booths." The reason is explained in Lev. 23:43. It was a teaching
tool to pass on Israel's faith to the next generation (cf. Exod. 12:26-27; 13:8,14; Deut. 6:1-2,7,20-25).

The word "foliage" in NASB is literally "fruit" (BDB 826). But the harvest is past so there would be
no fruit on the trees, yet they would still be "leafy."

The word "beautiful" (BDB 214) can mean

- ornament

- splendor

- honor

Here, it refers to either

- beautiful trees

- fruit trees

Israel made booths/huts of the branches of various leafy trees and decorated them with fruit (cf. Neh. 8:15).

▣ Notice there are four trees mentioned. Why four is unknown. These tree/palm branches were

- waved before the Lord (rabbinical tradition)

- made into booths (cf. Lev. 23:42-43; Neh. 8:13-18) or carried as festival sheaves (Lev. 23:40)

- these fruitless branches were a way to signal the harvest was over and a new agricultural cycle would begin

verses.zh: 每年七月间，要向耶和华守这节七日。这为你们世世代代永远的定例。
verses.en: You must celebrate it as a pilgrim festival to the Lord for seven days in the year. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations;[NOTE:1] you must celebrate it in the seventh month.
notes: Heb “for your generations.”

verses.zh: 你们要住在棚里七日；凡以色列家的人都要住在棚里，
verses.en: You must live in temporary shelters[NOTE:1] for seven days; every native citizen in Israel must live in shelters,
notes: Heb “in the huts” (again at the end of this verse and in v. 43), perhaps referring to temporary shelters (i.e., huts) made of the foliage referred to in v. 40 (J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 389).

verses.zh: 好叫你们世世代代知道，我领以色列人出埃及地的时候曾使他们住在棚里。我是耶和华―你们的　神。」
verses.en: so that your future generations may know that I made the Israelites live in shelters when I brought them out from the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.’”
verses.commentary:
23:43 "that your generations may know" The Hebrew VERB "know" (BDB 393, KB 390, Qal
IMPERFECT) has several senses (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW), but here it denotes two things.

- Know YHWH in a personal way that affects the way one lives.

- Know YHWH's will by knowing His law.

Both of these concepts are expressed by the VERB shema, which means
"to hear so as to do" (cf. Deut. 6:4; see full note online).

As with so many of Israel's feast days and cultus, living in "booths" was to provide an opportunity for
the adults to share with the children about the exodus (i.e., Deuteronomy 6).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation
of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Are the descriptions of the three major feasts described the same in Exodus, Leviticus, and Deuteronomy?

- Why was no work to be done on the Sabbath?

- Did Israel have two calendars?

- Were Passover and Unleavened Bread always combined into an eight-day feast?

- Does Lev. 23:9-15 go with 23:4-8? Why, why not.

- Does Lev. 23:9-15 refer to only the first year of entering Canaan or every year?

- How did the feasts of first fruits (Lev. 23:15-21) come to be called Pentecost?

- Is Lev. 23:23-25 a new year's festival?

- How is the Day of Atonement different from all the other special annual events?

verses.zh: 于是，摩西将耶和华的节期传给以色列人。
verses.en: So Moses spoke to the Israelites about the appointed times of the Lord.[NOTE:1]
notes: E. S. Gerstenberger (Leviticus [OTL], 352) takes v. 44 to be an introduction to another set of festival regulations, perhaps something like those found in Exod 23:14-17. For others this verse reemphasizes the Mosaic authority of the preceding festival regulations (e.g., J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 390).
